## 1) Run module-level AUB autopilot and select best
```bash
python3 experiment_system/tools/aub_autopilot.py --registry experiment_system/config/module_registry.yaml --run --select-best
```
**Goal:** Generate/score module variants and (if any clearly win) promote a new module config to “best” within the registry output artifacts.

**Check after it finishes:**
- A summary table of candidates vs champion with means/mins (or deltas).
- Whether it actually promoted anything (some runs will say “no candidate beats champion”).

## 2) Run system-level autopilot over system candidates
```bash
python3 experiment_system/tools/system_autopilot.py --spec experiment_system/config/system_candidates.yaml --run
```
**Goal:** Evaluate end-to-end system configs (often combinations of modules) and see if a full system candidate beats the current champion.

**Check after it finishes:**
- Which system candidate (if any) improved **tuning_mean/min** and/or **lockbox_mean/min**.
- Whether it reports statistical confidence / pass criteria (varies by harness).
- Any regressions masked by averages (e.g., mean improves but min collapses).

## 3) Generate the “next fix” plan/report
```bash
python3 experiment_system/tools/aub_next_fix.py --registry experiment_system/config/module_registry.yaml --output baseline/reports/next_fix.md
```
**Goal:** Produce an actionable shortlist of what to try next (likely based on where candidates fail or underperform).

**Check after it finishes:**
- That the report cites the latest run artifacts (not stale results).
- It should identify the weakest modules/areas and propose candidate edits.

---

- **lockbox_mean/min: 1.7925 / 1.1337** → min is much healthier; tail is less severe here.

So if new candidates improve mean slightly but further reduce **tuning_min**, you may want to reject unless your selection logic explicitly prioritizes mean over worst-case.

I can help decide whether any candidate truly beats the champion (and whether it’s a safe promotion given the mean/min tradeoffs).
